title: Revealing the Structure and Chemistry of Electrocatalysts during Reaction with Correlated Electrochemical Liquid Cell Electron and X-ray Microscopy
content: Electrochemical liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (EC-TEM) is a powerful tool for visualizing the structural transformations that occur in electrocatalysts under reaction conditions. Performing concurrent spatially resolved spectroscopic analysis of the same samples to obtain chemical state information is, however, not trivial because liquid layers with thicknesses in the several hundred nanometer range strongly attenuate the spectroscopic signatures. Correlative measurements with “broad-beam” techniques such as X-ray absorption spectroscopy or Raman spectroscopy, on the other hand, do not provide spatially resolved data, which limit the insight we can derive from these studies regarding local and minority structures. In this aspect, transmission soft X-ray microscopy (TXM) using the same EC-TEM liquid cells [1] has an intriguing potential to serve a bridge between high resolution microscopy and broad beam spectroscopy measurements.
